proposals.before: Sima Lun cast Emperor Hui into Jinyong and cynically rebranded the prison Yong'an.
proposals.after: Sima Lun cast Emperor Hui into Jinyong and renamed Jinyong Fortress the Yong'an Palace.
proposals.reason: 改號金墉城為永安宮: renamed it Yong'an Palace; no 'prison' or 'cynically' in source.

proposals.before: Haixi's cousin Yu Xi spent years croaking dirges and swinging a temple bell for accompaniment.
proposals.after: In the time of the Duke of Haixi, Yu Xi spent years croaking dirges and swinging a temple bell for accompaniment.
proposals.reason: 海西公時，庾晞: a time phrase; no kinship stated.

proposals.before: Taiyuan children clashed iron stakes in the mud in a game they named dòuzú.
proposals.after: In the Taiyuan era children clashed iron stakes in the mud in a game they named dòuzú.
proposals.reason: 太元中 is the Taiyuan era, not a place.

proposals.before: Sima Yan's Taihe 7 intercalary fifth month brought another da yu season.
proposals.after: Sima Yan's Taishi 7 intercalary fifth month brought another da yu season.
proposals.reason: 泰始七年 is Taishi 7.

proposals.before: Taikang 10's fourth month dried up again.
proposals.after: Taishi 10's fourth month dried up again.
proposals.reason: Still in the Taishi era (泰始十年).

proposals.before: An-di abdicated from Yong'an, won a hollow title at Pinggu, while Langya Wang Dewen became duke of Shiyang — both exiled to Xunyang.
proposals.after: An-di abdicated from Yong'an, won a hollow title at Pinggu, while Dewen, Prince of Langya, became duke of Shiyang — both exiled to Xunyang.
proposals.reason: 琅邪王德文: Prince of Langya named Dewen, not surname Wang.

proposals.before: Emperor An abdicated, left Yong'an Palace, was enfeoffed Prince of Pinggu; Langya Wang Dewen became Duke of Shiyang; both were ordered to reside in Xunyang city.
proposals.after: Emperor An abdicated, left Yong'an Palace, was enfeoffed Prince of Pinggu; Dewen, Prince of Langya, became Duke of Shiyang; both were ordered to reside in Xunyang city.
proposals.reason: 琅邪王德文: Prince of Langya named Dewen, not surname Wang.

proposals.before: The litany blames perennial drought on Sima Yan's trust in Jia, Xun, Yang, and Feng while excluding honest ministers.
proposals.after: The litany blames perennial drought on the trust placed in Jia Chong, Xun Xu, Yang Jun, and Feng Dan while excluding honest ministers.
proposals.reason: Source names 賈充、荀勖、楊駿、馮紞 and does not name Sima Yan.

proposals.before: Wang Jun's flotilla outran every rival to seize Nanjing.
proposals.after: Wang Jun's flotilla outran every rival to seize Moling.
proposals.reason: 秣陵 is Moling; anachronistic modern name.

proposals.before: "Monkling" was Sima Zhong's pet name.
proposals.after: "Monkling" was the crown prince's childhood name.
proposals.reason: 太子小名: the crown prince (Sima Yu), not Sima Zhong (Emperor Hui).

proposals.before: Sima Yi's bastards died by the purple-rein prophecy.
proposals.after: The Duke of Haixi was soon deposed; his three sons, said not to be his, were strangled with horse reins.
proposals.reason: Source names the Duke of Haixi; 'Sima Yi' collides with Sima Yi 懿.

proposals.before: Xiankang 2, twelfth month — a Hebei rhyme said, “Wheat enters the earth; kill Shi Wu.”
proposals.after: Xiankang 2, twelfth month — a Hebei rhyme said, “Wheat enters the earth; kill Shi Wu (Shi Hu).”
proposals.reason: 石武 stands for Shi Hu (taboo substitution).

proposals.before: Xiankang 2, twelfth month — a Hebei rhyme said, “Wheat enters the earth; kill Shi Wu.”
proposals.after: Xiankang 2, twelfth month — a Hebei rhyme said, “Wheat enters the earth; kill Shi Wu (Shi Hu).”
proposals.reason: 石武 stands for Shi Hu (taboo substitution).

proposals.before: Liu Yu's coup on 3/2 purged Xuan.
proposals.after: On the second day of the third month the righteous banners swept and secured the capital and executed Xuan.
proposals.reason: Source: 義旗以三月二日掃定京都，誅之 — no named 'coup' by Liu Yu.

proposals.before: Zhao's collapse followed the sign.
proposals.after: After Shi Jilong's fall the Central Plain turned toward Jin and generals and ministers were content.
proposals.reason: Source names 石季龍 and the Central Plain's submission.

proposals.before: Sima Yu and Yu fell the next year.
proposals.after: The next year Minhuai (the crown prince) was deposed and died.
proposals.reason: 湣懷廢死: one person, Crown Prince Minhuai.

proposals.before: Liu Yu struck Xiuzhi the year after.
proposals.after: The royal army attacked Sima Xiuzhi in the west the year after.
proposals.reason: 王旅西討司馬休之 names no commander.

proposals.before: Jia Nanfeng's minions fulfilled it.
proposals.after: Afterwards Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin took charge, leading to great disorder.
proposals.reason: Source: 孫秀、張林用事，遂至大亂.

proposals.before: Sima Dan's Wu income foretold his succession.
proposals.after: Emperor Kang, formerly Prince of Wu, still drew Wu commandery as his fief though moved to Langya — an image of his succeeding to the throne.
proposals.reason: 康帝 is Sima Yue 岳 (Emperor Kang), not 'Sima Dan'.

proposals.before: Tianxi's brief independence ended in Qin conquest.
proposals.after: Zhang Tianxi held sway in Liangzhou and soon surrendered to Fu Jian.
proposals.reason: Source: 張天錫稱雄於涼州，尋而降苻堅.

proposals.before: Gao Tang Long said: "This is Wei's great prodigy — guard against hawk-like ministers inside the screen wall."
proposals.after: Gaotang Long said: "This is Wei's great prodigy — guard against hawk-like ministers inside the screen wall."
proposals.reason: 高堂 is a compound surname: Gaotang Long.

proposals.before: Gao Tang Long said: "This is Wei's great prodigy — guard against hawk-like ministers inside the screen wall."
proposals.after: Gaotang Long said: "This is Wei's great prodigy — guard against hawk-like ministers inside the screen wall."
proposals.reason: 高堂 is a compound surname: Gaotang Long.

proposals.before: Li matched Huan's debased court.
proposals.after: Sun Liang lacked virtuous government and Sun Jun was arrogant and violent, matching Emperor Huan's case.
proposals.reason: Source: 孫亮未有德政，孫峻驕暴方甚，此與桓帝同事也.

proposals.before: Hui let his nephew be killed.
proposals.after: Emperor Hui, dull and unawakened, let Minhuai die that month.
proposals.reason: 湣懷 was Emperor Hui's son, not nephew.

proposals.before: Chu Ai and the minister framed Bo for logistics crimes.
proposals.after: At this time Rear General Chu Pou guarded Guangling and the chancellor proclaimed a northern campaign; Bo was executed under military law for transport delay and bribery.
proposals.reason: Source does not say framed; 褚裒 is Chu Pou.

proposals.before: Sima Yu was caged in first month.
proposals.after: In the first month of this year Crown Prince Minhuai was sent to be confined at the Xu palace.
proposals.reason: Source: 送湣懷太子，幽于許宮.

proposals.before: Liu Shan declared a new reign title while his father still lay unburied and the month unspent — another breach of what ritual language allowed.
proposals.after: Liu Bei died; Liu Shan mounted the throne; before the burial, before a month had passed, he changed the era name to Jianxing — another breach of what ritual language allowed.
proposals.reason: Source opens 劉備卒，劉禪即位; idiomatic omitted Liu Bei and the named succession.

proposals.before: No clever wordplay could spare him the doom that followed.
proposals.after: In the end Jiang Wei could not escape his fate.
proposals.reason: Source 維卒不免 names Jiang Wei; idiomatic omitted the person.

proposals.before: Yongxing opened with a frantic rearrangement: Tan demoted to Qinghe, Ying named imperial heir while hoarding every title Cao Cao once held.
proposals.after: In Emperor Hui's first Yongxing year an edict deposed Crown Prince Tan, restoring him as Prince of Qinghe, and established Prince Ying of Chengdu as imperial heir while he still held palace attendant, grand commander, chancellor, the nine bestowals, and twenty commanderies, on the model of the Wei king.
proposals.reason: Source names 惠帝、太子覃、清河王、成都王穎 and offices; idiomatic dropped them.

proposals.before: When speech and policy twist so wildly, the sovereign flees and the favorite prince dies — classic "presumption" blame.
proposals.after: When speech and policy twist so wildly, the emperor is driven into exile and Ying meets no good end — classic presumption blame.
proposals.reason: Source 穎亦不終 names Ying; idiomatic said only “favorite prince”.

proposals.before: Ming-di had fallen the previous new year.
proposals.after: Emperor Ming had fallen the previous new year.
proposals.reason: Source 明帝崩; restore Emperor Ming in idiomatic for EN coverage.

proposals.before: The move to Wuchang supplied the human overwork to match the omen.
proposals.after: At the time Sun Hao moved the capital to Wuchang — labor that stirred the masses to match the omen.
proposals.reason: Source 孫皓遷都武昌 names Sun Hao; idiomatic omitted him.

proposals.before: The conspirators acted on the ballad's hint.
proposals.after: Wang Ling and Linghu Yu heard the rhyme and plotted to enthrone Biao.
proposals.reason: Source 王淩、令狐愚…謀立彪 names the conspirators; idiomatic omitted them.

proposals.before: His corpse was treated exactly like the rhyme prescribed.
proposals.after: When Zhuge Ke died, they indeed wrapped him in a rush mat, bound his waist with bamboo strips, and cast him into the gravel pit.
proposals.reason: Source 諸葛恪死 names Zhuge Ke; idiomatic omitted him.

proposals.before: Zhuge Rong's suicide with the seal fulfilled the turtle omen.
proposals.after: Next year Zhuge Ke fell; his brother Rong held Gongan, was attacked, scraped the gold seal turtle and swallowed it — dying.
proposals.reason: Source names 諸葛恪 and 融; idiomatic kept only Zhuge Rong.

proposals.before: Nanfeng was the empress's sobriquet.
proposals.after: Nanfeng was Empress Jia's style name.
proposals.reason: Source 賈后字也; idiomatic said only “the empress”.

proposals.before: The allied princes purged Sima Lun within the year.
proposals.after: Within months the Prince of Qi, Chengdu, and Hejian righteous hosts jointly executed Lun.
proposals.reason: Source 齊王、成都、河間 names the three; idiomatic said only “allied princes”.

proposals.before: Ai-di perished in his prime, fulfilling the bitter rhymes.
proposals.after: Emperor Ai died young, fulfilling the bitter rhymes.
proposals.reason: Source 哀旁壽崩; restore Emperor Ai in idiomatic.

proposals.before: Commoners literally sowed wheat at his sealed portal.
proposals.after: When Duke Haixi was cast off, the people plowed his gate to plant wheat — thus the rhyme.
proposals.reason: Source 海西公被廢 names Duke Haixi; idiomatic omitted him.

proposals.before: The history notes his impotence and borrowed heirs.
proposals.after: Duke Haixi was not virile; he had attendants Xianglong and eunuchs couple to bear sons he claimed as his own.
proposals.reason: Source 海西公不男…向龍 names Duke Haixi and Xianglong; idiomatic paraphrased away.

proposals.before: The prophecy came true within the year.
proposals.after: Soon Zhongkan fell and Huan Xuan took Jingzhou.
proposals.reason: Source 仲堪敗，桓玄遂有荊州; restore names in idiomatic.

proposals.before: He died before taking Shitou.
proposals.after: Lu Long indeed lost and never entered Stone City.
proposals.reason: Source 盧龍果敗 names Lu Long; idiomatic said only “He”.

proposals.before: His kingship brought swift Wei suppression.
proposals.after: When Wenyi declared himself Yan king, Wei destroyed him.
proposals.reason: Source 文懿自立為燕王; restore Wenyi in idiomatic.

proposals.before: A dog soiled his throne-cloth.
proposals.after: Before Xuan emerged a dog defecated on his mat — all were astounded.
proposals.reason: Source 玄未及出 names Xuan; restore in idiomatic.

proposals.before: His courtiers quietly swapped the fouled seat.
proposals.after: Xuan was suspicious and violent; no one spoke; they drove off the dog and changed the mat.
proposals.reason: Source 玄性猜暴; restore Xuan in idiomatic.

proposals.before: The insult marked his illegitimate rule.
proposals.after: Heaven warns: Huan Xuan lacks virtue yet steals high place — hence the dog fouled his mat, showing how false his seat was.
proposals.reason: Source 桓玄無德; restore Huan Xuan in idiomatic.

proposals.before: His regime collapsed in eighty days.
proposals.after: Within eighty days Xuan fell and died.
proposals.reason: Source 玄敗亡; restore Xuan in idiomatic.

proposals.before: On dingsi in the fifth month of Taikang 5, two meteorites fell at Wen and two at Heyang.
proposals.after: In Emperor Wu's Taikang 5, fifth month, day dingsi, two meteorites each fell at Wen and Heyang.
proposals.reason: Source 武帝太康五年; restore Emperor Wu in idiomatic.

proposals.before: Flying timber decapitated a clerk — the wood-metal omen.
proposals.after: Late in Zhengshi under the King of Qi of Wei, Henan Yin Li Sheng's audience hall: a splinter sprang loose, struck clerk Shi Biao's head and severed it — wood harming metal.
proposals.reason: Source names 魏齊王、李勝、石彪; restore in idiomatic.

proposals.before: Officials prematurely asked to enshrine the living sovereign as "Mighty Ancestor" beside the dynasty's founding shrines, and the court assented.
proposals.after: In the first Jingchu year, the authorities memorialized that the emperor be titled Liezu and share, with Taizu and Gaozu, temples that would not be destroyed — and the court assented.
proposals.reason: Source names 烈祖、太祖、高祖; idiomatic paraphrased founding shrine titles away.

proposals.before: Qian Feng's ring around the capital failed; Su Jun and Liu Xia marched upriver from Huai-Si to lift the siege — matching where the rumor began.
proposals.after: When Qian Feng and Shen Chong's rebel hosts closed from four sides yet were broken by the imperial army, for over a month unable to ford the river, Northern Commandant Liu Xia and Huailing Neishi Sujun led Huai-Si troops to relieve the court — hence the rumor began in Huai-Si.
proposals.reason: Source names 錢鳳、沈充、劉遐、蘇峻; idiomatic dropped Shen Chong and softened others.

proposals.before: Soon two Wangs of one lineage tore the clan apart in open war.
proposals.after: Later Wang Guobao and Wang Xiaobo, of the same surname, attacked each other.
proposals.reason: Source 王國寶、王孝伯 names both; idiomatic said only “two Wangs”.

proposals.before: Worthy men languished in sinecures while mediocrities ran policy.
proposals.after: Moreover Li Xi, Lu Zhi, Li Yin and others all held idle posts — close to desired virtue unused.
proposals.reason: Source names 李憙、魯芝、李胤; idiomatic said only “worthy men”.

proposals.before: The palace had seized ministerial daughters the previous winter.
proposals.after: Last autumn and winter they drafted the daughters of Qing-xiao Zhuge Chong and others.
proposals.reason: Source 諸葛沖 names Zhuge Chong; idiomatic omitted him.

proposals.before: Yuankang 7's seventh month left Guanzhong buying grain at ten thousand cash a hu.
proposals.after: Seventh month of Emperor Hui's Yuankang 7 — great drought in Qin and Yong provinces, pestilence, Guanzhong famine, rice ten thousand cash per hu.
proposals.reason: Source 惠帝元康七年; restore Emperor Hui in idiomatic.

proposals.before: Yongjia 3 shriveled rivers until fords appeared on the great streams.
proposals.after: Emperor Huai's Yongjia 3, fifth month — great drought; rivers could be forded.
proposals.reason: Source 懷帝永嘉三年; restore Emperor Huai in idiomatic.

proposals.before: Warlords turned the heartland to slaughter — the drought's moral echo.
proposals.after: Moreover many lords harbored disloyal hearts; Liu Yuanhai, Shi Le, Wang Mi, Li Xiong and their ilk murdered the people until blood puddled as mud — also the drought's echo.
proposals.reason: Source names 劉元海、石勒、王彌、李雄; idiomatic said only “warlords”.

proposals.before: Jianwu 1's sixth month parched the lower Yangzi.
proposals.after: Emperor Yuan's Jianwu 1, sixth month — Yang Province drought.
proposals.reason: Source 元帝建武元年; restore Emperor Yuan.

proposals.before: Taixing 4's fifth month stayed dry.
proposals.after: Emperor Yuan's Taixing 4, fifth month — drought.
proposals.reason: Source 元帝太興四年; restore Emperor Yuan.

proposals.before: The deposed emperor's Taihe years opened with a summer drought.
proposals.after: Duke Haixi's Taihe 1 summer — drought.
proposals.reason: Source 海西公太和元年; restore Duke Haixi.

proposals.before: The annalist tied the weather to the Fei River aftermath and frontier sweeps.
proposals.after: At first, in the eighth year Fu Jian was broken; in the ninth generals raided territory — operations in Xu-Yu; Yang Liang and Zhao Tong campaigned against Ba-Mian.
proposals.reason: Source names 苻堅、楊亮、趙統; idiomatic paraphrased them away.

proposals.before: Xie An's redeployments kept the army in motion.
proposals.after: That year's first month Xie An again went out to garrison Guangling, sent his son Yan forward to Pengcheng — military service piled up.
proposals.reason: Source 謝安…子琰; restore Xie An and Yan.

proposals.before: Further outposts at Yewang thickened the military footprint.
proposals.after: That summer Guo Quan planted a garrison at Yewang and also sent troops to defeat Huang-Huai.
proposals.reason: Source 郭銓 names Guo Quan; idiomatic omitted him.

proposals.before: Sun En, Huan Xuan's double game, and Yuanxian's vanity threw the empire into military chaos.
proposals.after: At that time Sun En rebelled; Huan Xuan hesitated treacherously, forced Yin Zhongkan to his death, yet the court at once gave him Jingzhou; Sima Yuanxian also prompted the officials to honor him — inside and out were stirred, arms rose repeatedly.
proposals.reason: Source names 孫恩、桓玄、殷仲堪、司馬元顯; restore in idiomatic.

proposals.before: Sima Ye yielded in a hutment amid bean rows — the rhyme fulfilled.
proposals.after: By Jianxing 4 he surrendered to Liu Yao in a bean-patch redoubt east of the city.
proposals.reason: Source 帝降劉曜 names Liu Yao; idiomatic omitted him.

proposals.before: Xu Fu's mutiny matched the divination.
proposals.after: Later Wuxing's Xu Fu rebelled, killed prefect Yuan Xiu; Fu perished quickly — the answer.
proposals.reason: Source names 徐馥、袁琇; restore in idiomatic.

proposals.before: The deposed emperor moved into the very title foretold.
proposals.after: When Haixi was demoted to Prince of Donghai he then entered that mansion.
proposals.reason: Source 海西廢為東海王; restore Haixi in idiomatic.

proposals.before: On guisi in the fourth month of Taiyuan 13, after the rites were finished, a rabbit ran across the shrine hall.
proposals.after: Emperor Xiaowu, Taiyuan 13, fourth month, guisi — after the temple sacrifice was completed, a rabbit crossed the ancestral hall.
proposals.reason: Source 孝武太元十三年; restore Emperor Xiaowu.

proposals.before: The freak dog echoed Sima Yan's refusal to change the heir.
proposals.after: Heaven's warning: then the emperor ignored He Jiao's advice, finally enthroned Emperor Hui, inviting decay — punishment for heedless words.
proposals.reason: Source names 和嶠、惠帝; restore in idiomatic.

proposals.before: Subterranean barking yielded two pups in Wu commandery.
proposals.after: In Emperor Hui's Yuankang years a Lou county household heard puppy sounds underground; digging, they got a male and female.
proposals.reason: Source 惠帝元康中; restore Emperor Hui.

proposals.before: Huangfu Yan's western war brought mutiny and death.
proposals.after: Then Inspector Huangfu Yan campaigned against Wenshan Hu; aide He Lu counseled against it and was ignored; gate officer Zhang Hong exploited troop resentment, falsely accused Yan of treason, and killed him.
proposals.reason: Source names 皇甫晏、何旅、張弘; restore in idiomatic.

proposals.before: Fur grew from soil at Xiankang's start.
proposals.after: Early Emperor Cheng Xiankang — hair sprouted from earth — near white omen.
proposals.reason: Source 成帝咸康初; restore Emperor Cheng.

proposals.before: Thereafter Shi Hu fell and the Central Plain turned toward civilization; generals and ministers were content.
proposals.after: Thereafter Shi Jilong fell and the Central Plain turned toward civilization; generals and ministers were content.
proposals.reason: Literal must name 石季龍 as Shi Jilong (same person as idiomatic), not Shi Hu.

proposals.before: A six-month drought forced rites at every shrine from ancestors to rivers.
proposals.after: In the ninth year drought lasted from the first month through the sixth, and they prayed at the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, and the mountains and rivers.
proposals.reason: Restore ninth-year drought span (正月–六月) and the three prayer sites 宗廟/社稷/山川 omitted by the summary idiom.

proposals.before: The sites all tied to Wu and the future emperor.
proposals.after: Qu'a too was once Wu land; that the omen appeared at Wu Xiong's residence in a Wu town — was that not also Heaven's will?
proposals.reason: Restore 曲阿, 吳邑雄 (Wu Xiong), and the 天意 rhetorical question; drop invented “future emperor”.

proposals.before: Sima Wei's coup caught the new throne blind.
proposals.after: When the emperor had just taken the throne, Prince Chu Wei forged edicts to execute Prince Runan Liang and Grand Tutor Wei Guan, and the emperor could not see through it.
proposals.reason: 汝南王亮、太保衛瓘 must appear; 楚王瑋 is Prince Chu Wei, not a generic "coup."

proposals.before: The tree marked the whirl of four emperors.
proposals.after: When Xiaowu was only four, Ai soon died, Haixi took the throne and was soon deposed, Jianwen crossed from a prince's fief to inherit the great enterprise and ruled less than two years, then Xiaowu succeeded.
proposals.reason: 孝武、哀帝、海西、簡文 succession chain is explicit in 時孝武年始四歲…而孝武嗣統.

proposals.before: Twin black birds presaged Ming-di's death.
proposals.after: In Emperor Ming's eighth month, on gengxu, two great bluish-black birds with wings one zhang four chi wide appeared; one perched at the Minister of Education's residence and was shot dead, the other at a north-city household and was also taken.
proposals.reason: 明帝、司徒府、庚戌 omen facts are dropped; death is not stated in the unit.

proposals.before: Sima Teng marched toward Ye.
proposals.after: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Eastern Ying Teng Sima Teng moved his command from Bingzhou to garrison Ye, passing Zhengding en route.
proposals.reason: 東嬴王騰 and the march to 鄴 are explicit; Sima Teng alone omits title and route.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時帝初即位，楚王瑋矯詔誅汝南王亮及太保衛瓘，帝不能察。

decisions.reason: 孝武、哀帝、海西、簡文 succession chain is explicit in 時孝武年始四歲…而孝武嗣統.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時孝武年始四歲，俄而哀帝崩，海西即位，未幾而廢，簡文越自籓王，入纂大業，登阼享國，又不逾二年，而孝武嗣統。

sourceWitness.excerpt: 明帝八月庚戌，有大鳥二，蒼黑色，翼廣一丈四尺，其一集司徒府，射而殺之，其一集市北家人舍，亦獲焉。
